for callers waiting in a queue, executive insights by email, a page for messages that could not be delivered, mailboxes that recover by themselves, and fixes to transfers, email and reports.

Queue announcements: a voice queue can play its own message to waiting callers every so many seconds, in their chosen language, between the place and wait announcements and the hold music. When calls rise well above the queue's normal level, or there are too many callers for each free agent, a high-volume message takes its place by itself, supervisors are told, and it switches back once things settle. An emergency message, started from the Floor for some queues or all of them, plays at once to everyone already waiting and first to every new caller, until it is ended or its end time, at most 24 hours later. A banner shows on every screen while it plays.

Executive insights by email: under Scheduled reports, choose Executive insights and a campaign to have its report emailed every week or month. Each send makes a new version, attaches the one-page summary as a PDF and links to the full report.

Delivery problems: messages that could not be delivered have their own page under Omnichannel, for administrators, instead of on the Floor. It groups them by the mailbox or number they were sent from, says in plain words how to fix each reason, such as turning on Authenticated SMTP for a Microsoft mailbox, and shows whether each mailbox is being read.

Mailboxes that recover by themselves: when Microsoft or Google briefly refuses a mailbox's sign-in, the platform signs in again at once and tries again. A reply that is still refused waits and is tried again for about two hours instead of failing, and replies that failed this way go out by themselves once the mailbox works again. You are asked to sign in again only when the refusals keep coming. A busy mail server is no longer taken for a refused sign-in.

Live quality score on the Floor: hovering over a call's QA badge, or moving to it with the keyboard, opens a summary of the call's checklist: the score against the pass mark, each must-say line said or still to say, and how the customer seems.

Listening in the call library: agents can now play the calls in the call library without being allowed to hear every recording. A new permission, Listen to calls in the call library, is on the Agent role and opens only the library's calls; every playback is kept in the audit trail.

Save offers on chats and emails: when a customer writes one of your cancel phrases in a chat, WhatsApp, social message or email, the agent sees the same save offer they would on a call.

Executive insights in your language: the findings and recommendations are written in your organisation's language, and each report Yaxxa AI writes shows on your usage.

Retention drill-down and downloads: choose a figure on the Retention page to see the customers behind it, and download the report or any list as Excel or CSV. Value in another currency is shown apart, not converted.

Breaks in workforce figures: the Still on break? reminder follows the agent's scheduled break when they have one, and Agent time detail and Schedule adherence show the questions asked, how agents answered and the time worked while still on a break.

Fewer false quality alerts: a below-pass alert waits until enough of the form has been judged (half, unless you choose otherwise), must-say alerts with minutes arrive on time even during a silence, and alerts raised as a call ends close by themselves once the call is evaluated, or after a day.

Live quality score on chats and emails: the must-say and must-not-say lines on your quality form are now checked on chats, WhatsApp, social messages and emails too, ticking off as the agent writes them, with the same checklist on the desk, badge on the Floor and alerts.

Every report figure opens its records: on the standard reports, choose a count to see the calls, tickets, callbacks, evaluations, survey answers, leads, deal"}
